title: Entanglement of superpositions in zero-energy subspace: insights from stabilizer theory
abstract: Exact zero-energy eigenstates built from entangled dimers have recently been found in a large class of spin Hamiltonians. While the individual states have a simple structure, their superpositions can have very different entanglement properties. In this work, we study these superpositions for geometrically local spin-1/2 chains with periodic boundary conditions. Using stabilizer theory and polynomial methods, we characterize the subspace they span and find the minimum entanglement entropy between two halves of the chain. For Hamiltonians generated by a single local Pauli interaction with noncommuting translates, this minimum obeys a volume law at fixed interaction range. The structure of the least-entangled superpositions also suggests further exact eigenstate constructions, including zero-energy states separable between the two halves of the chain and states at nonzero energies.
summary: This work analyzes the entanglement properties of superpositions of zero-energy eigenstates in spin chains using stabilizer theory. By optimizing the entanglement entropy over the spanned subspace, the authors determine scaling laws for the minimum entanglement. The results provide new insights into the structure of the zero-energy manifold and suggest methods for constructing additional exact eigenstates.
main_problem: The paper investigates the entanglement properties of superpositions formed from exact zero-energy eigenstates within a constrained subspace of spin Hamiltonians.
main_result: For certain Hamiltonians, the minimum entanglement entropy across a chain bipartition obeys a volume law, and the analysis reveals methods to construct other exact eigenstates, including those with zero entanglement.
method: The study employs stabilizer theory and polynomial methods to characterize the spanned subspace and optimize the entanglement entropy over all possible superpositions.
model_or_system: The focus is on geometrically local spin-1/2 chains with periodic boundary conditions, governed by Hamiltonians that are sums of local Pauli interactions.
key_observables: Minimum entanglement entropy (half-chain entanglement entropy), the structure of the least-entangled superpositions, and the scaling of entanglement with system size.
important_parameters: Fixed interaction range, system size L, and the specific form of the local Pauli interaction terms.
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily focuses on the subspace spanned by antipodal states, which may not cover the entire zero-energy eigenspace.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the structure of the zero-energy eigenstate as a tensor product of entangled dimers on antipodal sites.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the entanglement optimization problem, using stabilizer theory to characterize the subspace, deriving the minimum entanglement entropy, and then using the structure of the least-entangled states to propose new exact eigenstate constructions.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of stabilizer theory to entanglement optimization in lattice models provides powerful tools for understanding ground state properties and entanglement structure in strongly correlated quantum systems.
